purpose: Trace the first-playable route and prove progression/return ownership before conversion to matter-state traversal.

findings.finding: Route crossing remains centralized in LocalCellBoundaryMorphSystem rather than in Grave/Vascular/Silt route gameplay systems.
findings.implication: HC019B must preserve this crossing authority and make it consume material/world state; it should not create a second transition owner.

findings.finding: Interact-driven return recipes share generic boundary handling.
findings.implication: The HOTFIX1 re-arm guard addresses same-press return risk globally, but the next playtest must verify the exact route that returned to Hub because multiple return recipes can pass through the same authority.

findings.finding: The current route architecture still separates route completion truth from crossing truth.
findings.implication: This is structurally useful, but it is also the source of the 'objective/flag then transition' feel. HC019B should change what completion observes, not who owns crossing.

findings.finding: HC018 material/verb systems are presentation and local-state layers around existing progression rather than the sole progression cause.
findings.implication: The next implementation pass should convert exactly one early-route obstacle so material state becomes the causal prerequisite.

findings.finding: No evidence justifies deleting generic boundary authority or rewriting all routes in HC019A.
findings.implication: This pass intentionally makes no gameplay fix beyond the already-applied HC018E HOTFIX1.
